dehydrated_text:
So we've done the Greeks and Israelites, and today we discuss the Persians and introduce Zoroaster, who is said to be the most influential person ever. He will create Zoroastrianism, the world's first great religion, leading to the rise of the Persian Empire.

Intuitively, we understand the universe as conscious, vibrating infinitely. Lower vibrations manifest in matter, giving rise to humans. Our minds inhabit the spiritual realm, constantly dialoguing with the universe. This concept is hard to grasp, so we use metaphors or stories to explain it.

God, known as the Monad, is perfect but lacks imagination and creativity. When God emanates, He creates imperfect humans—material beings capable of pain, fallibility, and creativity. Both God and humanity are in a process of becoming perfection through eternity and infinity, co-creators with God.

Free will is essential for true creativity; without it, there can be no genuine innovation. The individual's internal experience matters because only we can foster creativity by interacting with the Monad. A metaphor likens us to mirrors around a candle, reflecting its light within us.

Eternity and reincarnation are key concepts: upon death, consciousness returns to the spirit world for reflection. If you've been virtuous, you ascend; if not, you remain in lower realms. This influences ideas of heaven and hell, allowing for self-reflection and recognition of one's impact on the world.
